review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked it only against the repeated-proof-machinery rubric. Most of the repetition is in thin wrappers. The nndist lemmas are all `NNReal.eq <| dist_...`. The swapped-argument variants use `dist_comm` and one existing lemma. The lineMap and homothety distance lemmas each need only a short simp or rw calculation. These are too short to justify a shared lemma.

The closest candidate is the four Metric.image_homothety_{ball, closedBall, closedBall_of_nonneg, sphere_of_nonneg} proofs. Each has the shape `rw [image_homothety, IsometryEquiv.image_X, smul_X, IsometryEquiv.image_X]; simp [homothety_apply]`. The scalar-action lemma differs each time (`smul_ball`, `smul_closedBall'`, `smul_closedBall`, `smul_sphere`). So do the hypotheses: `hx : x ≠ 0` in some, `hr : 0 ≤ r` with `Nontrivial W` in others. A unifying helper would need to be generic over the set family, and the shared reasoning is already factored into the private `image_homothety`. A wrapper lemma would add machinery without removing nontrivial reasoning, so I did not report it. I also did not report `image_homothety_sphere`, which reduces to ball and closedBall via a set difference. I did not find any other nontrivial repeated mathematical argument. Nothing was left unreviewed. The only uncertainty is that I did not test the possible abstractions for the image-of-ball proofs.
